== Biography ==
Thomas Glasgow, husband of [[Davidson-14073|Christian (Christine) Davidson]], belonged to the Livingston and Blackburn family recorded in parish baptisms from 1774. He is confidently, though inferentially, identified with the Thomas baptised on 2 February 1746 at Davistoun to [[Glasgow-1023|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Mill-357|Janet Mill]]. On that identification he was born before that day; the baptism does not establish an exact birthday.<ref name="Davistoun1746" />

A Livingston marriage index records their marriage on or after 7 November 1772 at Livingston. It is a reported banns/marriage index date, not a newly inspected ceremony record.<ref name="Marriage1772">Church of Scotland: Old Parish Registers, Banns and Marriages, Livingston parish 669, reference 20/81, frame 497, Christan Davidson and Thomas Glasgow, on or after 7 November 1772; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ ScotlandsPeople index], accessed 3 September 2026. No original newly inspected.</ref>

Their recorded family includes [[Glasgow-1452|Nathaniel]], baptised 2 January 1774; [[Glasgow-1448|Janet]], baptised 2 February 1777; [[Glasgow-1451|Catharine]], born 20 August and baptised 31 August 1780 at Blackburne; [[Glasgow-1453|Mary]], indexed at Livingston in 1783 with variant dates discussed below; [[Glasgow-1449|Thomas]], whose OPR derivative gives birth 26 April 1787 and baptism 6 May at Whitburn, residence Blackburn; and [[Glasgow-1450|Peter]], recorded in the family’s 1790 baptism sequence.<ref name="FamilyParish">Held parish derivatives: Nathaniel, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685841078&tab=this R_685841078] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692405171&tab=this R_692405171]; Janet, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685844147&tab=this R_685844147] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692403113&tab=this R_692403113]; Catharine, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4152175&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/4152175] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685841001&tab=this R_685841001], with [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1R2-KBV FamilySearch X1R2-KBV]; Mary, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685840887&tab=this R_685840887] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692403782&tab=this R_692403782]; younger Thomas, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4171361&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/4171361], [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685840829&tab=this R_685840829] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692406064&tab=this R_692406064]. Full Thomas Glasgow/Christian Davidson couple stated; companion entries for one event are not independent witnesses. Original registers uninspected.</ref> Nathaniel is the first child in the held sequence; this does not prove he was the eldest.

Christian probably died on 5 November 1795, the date shared by the memorial derivatives, which disagree over whether she was 43 or 45. Thomas's preferred death year is 1831, aged 85, with 22 May and 22 July retained as competing readings. The inherited 22 May 1851 reading remains an alternative rather than being silently discarded. Their daughter Janet is probably the memorial's daughter who died on 16 October 1853; the companion 1873 reading is preserved below.<ref name="LivingstonFamilyMI" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Thomas's childhood and father assessment ===
The preferred identification is with Thomas baptised at Davistoun, Livingston, on 2 February 1746, son of [[Glasgow-1023|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Mill-357|Janet Mill]]. The explicit recorded-child father clause retains its narrower 98% assessment; the complete adult-to-father placement was reviewed at 78% probable on 23 October and is now assessed at 93% confident inference. These are different scopes, not independent confirmations or percentages to multiply. Janet Kilpatrick belongs to the older Thomas's parental generation, not as a competing wife or this child's mother.<ref name="Davistoun1746">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Thomas Glasgow, baptism 2 February 1746, Livingston, residence Davistoun, parents Thomas Glasgow and Janet Mill, OPR 669/1 item 4; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4151556&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/4151556]. Held derivative; original register uninspected. Retained FamilySearch citation [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RG-JFP X1RG-JFP].</ref>

The 1831/age-85 reading implies birth approximately in 1745–1746 and coheres with this baptism, the same parish and the later Christian Davidson family. In contrast, the calculated 1766 birth would make the father only about seven or eight at Nathaniel's 1774 baptism. This supports preferring the coherent reading without treating the two Findmypast versions as independent votes. A correct 1851 death with an incorrect age, a different similarly aged Thomas, or a mistaken childhood attribution remain possible.

Named weaker comparisons are [[Glasgow-1413|Thomas Glasgow]], born 3 January and baptised 8 January 1744 at Irvine to [[Glasgow-1410|Michael Glasgow]] and [[Crauford-31|Mary Crauford]], and [[Glasgow-4109|Thomas Glasgow]], born 12 January and baptised 9 February 1749 at Edinburgh to [[Glasgow-3582|John Glasgow]] and [[Morrison-24595|Eliz Morison/Morrison]]. They would be 87 and 82 respectively in May/July 1831, fitting the memorial's age 85 less closely and lacking the same parish continuity. Neither is excluded by absent later-life fields, and neither receives a new individual percentage.

=== Recorded children and later identity limits ===
Catharine's father placement was raised from 71% to 97% on 23 October when the held OPR derivative's full parental couple and Blackburne dates were reconciled. Peter's recorded-child father assessment remains 97%. Nathaniel, Mary and younger Thomas are now each assessed at 97% for their parish-defined father relationships, replacing 68%, 70% and 69% respectively. These grades identify the adult Thomas/Christian household, not the father's childhood or all later lives of the children. Their maternal questions are assessed separately; Janet's existing mother placement is individually rated at 97%. No new father or mother attachment, adult merger or live WikiTree save follows from the review.

Mary's Livingston companions give baptism 29 June 1783; OPR 669/1 item 4 gives birth 18 May 1783 at Blackburn but baptism 29 June 1784; Whitburn companions give 6 July 1783, all with Thomas and Christian Davidson. These discrepancies remain unresolved; neither a silent year correction nor additional children follow from them.<ref name="MaryVariants">Held Findmypast derivatives [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4152265&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/4152265], [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685856989&tab=this R_685856989] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692420222&tab=this R_692420222]; original entries uninspected.</ref> The younger Thomas's companions label 26 April 1787 as baptism at Livingston, while the Whitburn OPR labels it birth and gives baptism 6 May; its page 61 and Blackburn residence are retained. The full couple agrees despite differing event labels.

A further Peter was indexed as born 11 January and baptised 31 May 1793 at Livingston to Thomas Glasgow, labourer; no mother is supplied, OPR 669/1 item 4. If both explicit birth dates are correct, this cannot simply be the selected 1790 baptism child. The ambiguous adult history under Peter-1450 is not excluded by an estimated year. Thomas-1382 remains only a qualified father-role comparison for the 1793 entry; no mother or new child attachment is invented.<ref name="Peter1793">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4152404&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/4152404], held inspected derivative, 30 October 2026; original uninspected.</ref>

Nathaniel's Kingsessing/Leith comparisons, Mary's Thomson/1871 Bridgeton comparisons, and younger Thomas's Sarah Chapman/Henry 1880 material remain separately qualified in their accounts. The present family argument does not resolve them.

=== Janet's identity and parental roles ===
The held Livingston baptism names Janet Glasgow, Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson on 2 February 1777; one companion gives Livingston residence. These are two indexes of one event, not separate children.<ref name="Janet1777">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685844147&tab=this R_685844147] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692403113&tab=this R_692403113], Janet Glasgow, baptism 2 February 1777, Livingston, parents Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson; held inspected derivatives, original register uninspected.</ref> The memorial explicitly calls Christian Janet's mother and Thomas her father. The full couple, family memorial and chronology support 97% for each existing parent placement. The father's former 43% possible grade is superseded; the mother's 97% is her first individual rating, not a new maternal attachment or a measured rise from an invented earlier percentage.

Age 76 with death in 1853 is compatible with baptism near birth in 1777, although baptism need not have been in infancy. The conflicting 1873/76 combination implies birth around 1797, after the named mother's 1795 death, so those digits cannot all be correct for the same daughter. A correct later death year with a wrong age remains possible. The combined correlation favours 16 October 1853, with 1873 remaining an alternative.

The inherited Bridgeton, Kincardineshire birthplace remains unverified and is retained as a field-level claim, not asserted by the Livingston baptism. The fuller inscription's “Janet Glasgow, Blackburn” may identify a locality; it does not prove a married surname. No husband, marriage or descendants are inferred. An earlier about-1780 birth estimate and firm unsourced parent statement were superseded by the existing before-2-February-1777 bound and the dated assessments. The present family inference replaces the older blanket hold; it does not silently settle the place or surname questions.

=== Memorial readings and source limits ===
The preferred readings come from a combined interpretation of held derivatives, not a new stone reading or source fetch. One Findmypast version gives Thomas's death as 22 July 1831, aged 85; Christian Davidson, 5 November 1795, aged 43; son Peter, 12 September 1810, aged 19; and daughter Janet, 16 October 1853, aged 76. It also names grandchildren Mary Russell, who died in infancy, Jessie Russell, 11 July 1845, aged 20, another Jessie Russell, 8 February 1851, aged ten months, and James B. Russell, 22 April 1854, aged nineteen months.

The fuller companion says Janet Glasgow, Blackburn, erected the memorial for her mother Christian Davidson, who died 5 November 1795 aged 45; Thomas Glasgow her father, 22 May 1831 aged 85; and Peter her brother, 12 September 1819 aged 48. It gives the above Janet's death as 16 October 1873 aged 76, the infant Jessie's date as 8 February 1831, and James B. Russell's year as 185*. These differing month/year/age readings are retained, not harmonised into independent people or new exact facts. Repeated rows under different family names still refer to the same memorial.<ref name="LivingstonFamilyMI">Findmypast, ''Scotland Monumental Inscriptions'', Livingston family memorial, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00542646&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00542646] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511333&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511333]; compare the same inscription indexed under Janet as [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00422894&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00422894] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511321&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511321], and under Peter as [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00516377&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00516377] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511329&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511329]. Held derivative transcriptions captured/reviewed 24–30 October 2026; one physical memorial, not independent witnesses. [https://billiongraves.com/grave/Thomas-Glasgow/3399144 BillionGraves memorial 3399144, marker LV 106] has a competing 1851 Thomas reading and a previously blurred preview; original inscription not newly read.</ref>

BillionGraves instead indexes Thomas's death as 22 May 1851, aged 85, from which the earlier circa-1766 birth was calculated. That is not an independent birth record. The original stone and parish-register images remain uninspected for this reconciliation. A legible inscription or burial record could resolve the disputed digits, but a blanket requirement for an original does not prevent a qualified preferred interpretation of the existing family evidence. No Russell grandchild is assigned a parent profile through these readings alone.

=== Assessment history and remaining work ===
On 22 October the recorded 1746 child relationship was assigned 98%; on 23 October the complete adult placement was reduced to 78% to distinguish that identity scope. The 30 October reconciliation now supports 93% for the complete placement while retaining the conditional 98% and the former 78% with their actual bases. The old calculated circa-1766 birth and 1851 death reading remain source history; the present preferred interpretation is stated above. The old requirement to defer every inference until the original is superseded, not the record of its earlier uncertainty. No new original, source fetch or proof of Thomas-1023's own earlier identity is claimed.

[https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/people/glasgow-1382.html#research-findings Full current family argument]. The next useful evidence is a legible inscription or burial record for disputed digits and original parish residence/witness details for the remaining childhood-to-adult identity question.
